candidates.exact_span: The State of New Mexico and Navajo Nation WQS criteria applicable to the warm-water aquatic life designated use are at least 5 mg/L and 6 mg/L, respectively, for dissolved oxygen.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretation of which receiving-water DO criterion (5 mg/L vs 6 mg/L) applies to the discharge could change which numeric standard is used when evaluating reported DO measurements against applicable limits.

candidates.exact_span: to develop permit parameters for the protection of the State of New Mexico surface water WQS for DO (i.e., 5 mg/L).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this passage is read as selecting only the New Mexico 5 mg/L criterion (versus the Navajo Nation 6 mg/L criterion also mentioned) could change which DO-related limit is treated as enforceable for compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: various BOD5 factors including BOD5 Secondary Treatment Standards were considered and simulated to achieve the DO criterion.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether Secondary Treatment Standards set a floor or alternative basis for BOD5 limits could change which enforceable numeric BOD5 limit is deemed applicable when comparing reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Primarily based on the City of Farmington Wastewater Treatment Plant's design flow of 6.67 MGD (0.292 m3/s)) and the receiving water critical flow of 431.3 cfs (278.6 MGD), various BOD5 factors including BOD5 Secondary Treatment Standards were considered and simulated to achieve the DO criterion.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If design flow or critical low-flow assumptions are treated as operative permit conditions rather than modeling background, a different interpretation of whether actual flows match these values could change which derived BOD5 limits are considered applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Other effluent parameters provided in the permittee's application and applied in the model include Ammonia (Avg: 8 mg/L), DO (Avg: 5.63 mg/L), temperature (23 C), Nitrate plus Nitrite Nitrogen (Avg: 20 mg/L), T. Phosphorus (2.9 mg/L) and E. Coli (Avg: 4 MPN/100 mL).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether these application values are read as establishing enforceable effluent limits versus model-input assumptions could change which numeric limits are applied when evaluating reported measurements for those parameters.

candidates.exact_span: The model results show no excursion of the receiving stream DO standard of 6 mg/L when the BOD5 limits of 30 mg/l for monthly average and 45 mg/l for 7-day maxima were applied (see graph with 30/45 mg/L BOD5 in Appendix 1; other detail information is available upon request).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage states the operative BOD5 numeric limits (30 mg/l monthly average; 45 mg/l 7-day maxima) and ties them to a 6 mg/L receiving-water DO standard; different readings of which limit form applies (monthly average vs 7-day maxima) or which DO standard governs could change limit applicability and the monitoring/averaging obligations implied by those limit forms.

candidates.exact_span: A complete characterization of San Juan River (i.e., water quality and hydrodynamic data) was not available. Where data were not available, estimates and assumptions are made.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of this as a documented no-data/assumption state versus unresolved applicability could change how missing or non-numeric monitoring evidence is classified when no ordinary reported result is available.

candidates.exact_span: receiving stream average depth of 6 feet (2 meters) were assumed since no data available.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this is treated as an explicitly documented assumption filling a data gap versus evidence that remains unresolved could change the established missing-evidence state for related monitoring or modeling inputs.

candidates.exact_span: The model results are based on the assumptions and default values as explained and presented above. Should these conditions change, the model should be updated to provide a more accurate assessment of the water quality within the receiving water body.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether changed conditions trigger a different operative limit set or only a future modeling update could change current limit applicability (A) and whether present missing or conditional-evidence cases should be classified as documented conditional non-requirement versus unresolved (C).
